name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: require/check verb is the domain action; 'char_id_in_active_party' precisely names what is verified (a char_id present in the live battle party). No Ghidra address residue. Param is the required char_id (low byte), NOT a class/job id, so this name (which replaced the old misnomer fd2_check_party_has_required_class) is correct. Also disambiguated from the menu/template-scope fd2_check_party_has_char_id @ 0x33499 by 'active_party'.
purpose: Verify a required char_id is present in the live battle party (runtime_char_array slots 1..max_chars); on a miss show a 'you need [char-name]' portrait dialog and return 0, on a hit return 1 silently.
logic_summary: found=0; for iter in [0,max_chars): if data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr[iter+1].char_id == (uint8)req_char_id then found=1 (slot 0 is the always-present lord, skipped via the +1 offset; only player-selected slots 1..max_chars are checked). If found==0: fd2_load_chapter_portrait(0x4B); set data_fd2_dialog_last_action_sprite_id_param = (req_char_id&0xFF)+1 (per-char dynamic portrait slot); fd2_display_dialog_scene(all_game_text,0x291,0xA951F,0x140,0xCD,0x4C,0x4A,0x13,1) renders the 'you need [name]' scene; fd2_paint_portrait_to_dialog_area(0); raise input guard data_fd2_battle_tile_map_ptr=1; fd2_wait_for_input_dialog_with_blink(0); lower guard=0; fd2_close_intro_dialog_with_slide_out(). Return found. Compiler __CHK(0x30) stack-probe prologue.

params.name: max_chars
params.semantics: Active-party iteration cap = number of non-lord party slots to scan. Caller passes 0x0F (current_chapter_id <= 0x1A) or 0x13 (> 0x1A). Loop scans runtime_char_array[1..max_chars].
params.reason: Name matches caller's own 'max_chars' variable and accurately describes the iteration cap. No address residue.

params.name: req_char_id
params.semantics: Required char_id (only low byte used); compared against each runtime slot's char_id field, and used as (req_char_id&0xFF)+1 to pick the per-char error-portrait slot. Caller supplies chapter-specific char_ids (0x12, 9, 0x10, 0x15, 0x18, 0x1D) from its branch table.
params.reason: Name correctly states this is a char_id (not a class/job id) and that it is the value being required. No address residue.

returns.semantics: 1 = required char_id found in active party (no dialog). 0 = missing (error dialog was shown). Caller stores it into result_flag, which gates whether the recruitment commit proceeds.
